guide.summary: User (OAuth 2.0) app, basic scopes (approval path unconfirmed); Server app (JWT or CCG), per-customer admin (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)); Scopes available only on request (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)). guide.verdict: Easiest: Server app (JWT or CCG), per-customer admin (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)). Hardest: Scopes available only on request (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)).

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Box app. For production you will likely want your own app so users see your brand and you get your own quota.

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: You need a Box developer account with Developer Console access. A free one works for testing.

prerequisites.title: Choose app type first
prerequisites.detail: An OAuth 2.0 app cannot be switched to Server Authentication, or the reverse. You would have to create a new app.

steps.title: Create the Box app
steps.detail: In the Developer Console choose New App, then User (OAuth 2.0) or Server (JWT or CCG).

steps.title: Prepare redirect URI and scopes
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and check it is HTTPS. Draft the minimal scope list.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI and scopes are ready to paste.

steps.title: Enter redirect URI and scopes in Box
steps.detail: Set these on the Configuration tab. Add scopes before any admin authorizes the app.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use the Composio API to create a custom Box auth config with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Customer admin authorizes the app
steps.detail: The admin adds the app in the Admin Console Platform Apps tab using your Client ID, or enables it for OAuth apps.
inputs: Client ID sent to the admin

steps.title: Open support ticket for special scopes
steps.detail: Request the scope through Box support from a paid enterprise account. An agent can draft the use-case justification.

traps.title: Config changes force re-authorization
traps.detail: After authorization, changing scopes or access level needs the admin to re-authorize before tokens reflect it.

traps.title: Unpublished apps may be disabled by default
traps.detail: If the customer's admin turned on 'Disable unpublished apps by default', your OAuth app will not work until enabled.

traps.title: Managed app limits in production
traps.detail: The managed app shows Composio on the consent screen and shares quota with all Composio users.

traps.title: Usage counts against customer's API allocation
traps.detail: Custom app calls, including authentication requests, count toward the customer's monthly allocation. Box AI calls use separate AI Units.

blockers.symptom: Customer admin has not approved the app and is waiting.
blockers.what_it_means: Box cannot speed up admin authorization.
blockers.what_to_do: Send the admin your Client ID and instructions, then follow up.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin instructions and email.

blockers.symptom: Extra scope request is refused or unavailable.
blockers.what_it_means: Requests are reviewed one by one, and a free trial account cannot request them.
blockers.what_to_do: Use a paid enterprise account and explain why the scope is needed.
